## SmallPen operation rules

Use the supplied CLI path, otherwise `smallpen` on PATH. The CLI's help/schema is complete without a Skill. Discover operations with `help`, then `help OBJECT`, `help OBJECT ACTION`, and the returned schema queries. Read only the action and input fields needed now; use returned IDs, not invented selectors. Put write JSON in files.

Start with one target and compact text. Search large result files with file tools instead of loading the full result into context. Decode JSON text, preserve LF newlines and spaces, and display wireframes in monospace without soft wrapping. Request PNG inspection only when useful and the caller accepts images; a text-only caller may export PNG but must not claim to have inspected it.

Supply a stable batch ID before retryable edits, reuse it only with identical input, and read the write receipt. Follow scoped error recovery and current schemas. An explicit reverse edit is a new guarded write; it is not history rollback. Read check issues, skipped coverage and rendering limits before describing a result as verified.

These are tool rules. The scene below defines how to use the tool for this task.

## CLI rules from source

- CLI version: 0.1.0-alpha.7. Use the installed CLI's help/schema when its version differs.
- Replies are compact JSON with a 8 KiB budget. Large complete results use resultFile paths; --full expands data, while --stdout explicitly requests large stdout.
- Temporary results have unique names in one system temporary directory. Each invocation cleans managed files older than 30 minutes. Read them promptly; --output keeps requested deliverables.
- When the project uses Tokens: No --theme: use each project's group defaults, never the App's active selection. Libraries without stored defaults use the real Default option, else the first option in library order.
- Project defaults < explicitly requested Scenario themes < explicit --theme. Override only named groups; unspecified groups keep defaults. Presentation chooses structure and does not implicitly choose a theme.
- Groups and options are project-defined. Platform, language, light/dark, brand and density are examples, never required dimensions or fixed flags. --locale changes CLI labels only.
- token theme default --theme Group/Option explicitly saves a project default; the App's own active selection changes only in the App (or with a set-active-token-themes operation through advanced apply). View, validate and export never save a selection.
- Scoped checks: Validate canonical data and report text/layout/contrast issues and coverage; a page checks every version and a component every variant unless one is named.

# Application design

Deliver an editable SmallPen package, its design system, requested prototype connections and scoped review results. Application implementation belongs to the later development task.

## Understand the project

On first use, establish what software the user wants, who uses it, the core tasks and content, the expected platforms, and which platform to deliver first. Ask about missing choices that affect scope, structure or behavior. Use answers already supplied; a complete brief can proceed without another approval round. Bundle related questions. Keep the user's language unless the project requires another one.

Inspect an existing package before adding definitions. Maintain one `DESIGN.md` alongside the package, updating it rather than creating a file each round. Record confirmed requirements, the first platform, capabilities each platform must preserve, style direction, names, shared definitions, justified structural differences and review targets/combinations. Mark assumptions and sample data. Missing key requirements require questions; ordinary visual details can be chosen and recorded.

## Tokens, components, then pages

Work by name. Use `token` for design values (including colors, typography and font choice) and `token theme` for their groups, options and defaults. Theme options are always `Group/Option`, the same name a Token value uses: `token theme add --theme Viewport/Tablet` adds one (and its group when new), and `token theme rename`, `token theme default`, `token theme delete` take the same names. Use `token set` for Tokens and their option values (strings for UI text are `string` Tokens in a language group, bound as `"text": "{text.path}"`; `boolean` Tokens bound to `visible` show or hide an element per option), `component define` for a component with its properties and variant changes, `page draw` for a page or one container, `flow link`, `flow unlink` and `flow start` for prototype links (`--platform` picks the page version; `flow list` shows them; an element inside a copy links as `"Page / Copy / Element"`), `page rename`/`page delete` (`--element` for one element, `--platform` for one version), `component rename` (`--element` renames an element in every variant) and `component delete` (`--variant` deletes one variant), `page move --direction up|down|left|right` to rearrange, `page set` and `component set` to change some fields of one element (or of the page or component itself: `--set width=320 --set fill={color.surface}`, a copy's `props`/`text`) without drawing it again (name the version or variant with `--platform`/`--variant` when the element is in several; `--all` only when every one should change); never compute coordinates yourself: the CLI places elements and keeps them from overlapping. All pages share one canvas laid out in rows (one row block per module, `Tasks / ...` pages left to right from the start page along links); split pages onto another canvas only when asked or clearly separate (`canvas put`), because links and prototype flows only work within one canvas. Write `{token.path}` to bind a Token. The bundled font covers Latin only: for Chinese or another script, import a font into the package with `asset font import` and use it through a font-family Token with `"fontFamily": "{font.family.base}"`. Names never repeat: give sibling elements, pages, components, canvases and colors their own names (unnamed elements are numbered for you); a rename onto a used name is numbered ("Card 2") as in the App; a name stored twice shows in `view --as issues`, and `"Name [2]"` picks one to rename. No command needs an ID and replies show none.

Read existing theme groups, raw Token definitions and components. Define the needed shared vocabulary before drawing pages: typography, colors, spacing, radii, borders and useful reusable dimensions. Groups are project-defined; do not require a platform, language or light/dark group. Add a platform group only if this project's value differences need it. Create or reuse Tokens, then bind them when creating the components and nodes. Check actual bindings; an inventory of unused Tokens is not a design system. Do not leave design Token binding work for the developer. Task-specific geometry can remain literal where a Token has no useful meaning.

Build shared navigation, headers, inputs, actions and business-content components, then compose their instances on pages. Express component states, sizes and suitable structural alternatives as variants of one component. Labels such as Save and Cancel use instance text overrides rather than separate component definitions. Compose standard shell parts and content instances in a page frame. The current instance API does not expose an arbitrary content slot; do not insert business children under an instance and assume they replace its source subtree.

For a new package, discover `project init`. It creates a blank package with no pages (`page draw` makes the first); it does not decide the business requirements, theme dimensions or platform page copies. Configure the first requested design explicitly.

## Adapt the same content

Deliver the agreed first platform, then assess the later platforms against the same business content and capabilities. Do not automatically create Desktop and Mobile copies of every page.

Use the smallest change the requested difference needs:

1. Keep the same page/content structure and use Token combinations for bound value changes: widths, heights, padding, gaps, type and color. Set the values for the chosen project groups. Check the same page with the appropriate explicit combination.
2. Use component variants for local reusable structural differences that values cannot express. A Token combination does not automatically select a component variant.
3. Add a Presentation or separate page only when the overall structure or interaction differs substantially and cannot be expressed through the shared design. Record the reason and preserve shared components and content.

Tokens cannot currently switch visibility, layout direction or node trees. Consult `schema node`, operation schemas and projection diagnostics before relying on layout support. If required behavior exceeds tool support, report the specific gap and ask about the affected design choice; do not silently duplicate full pages or omit functionality to pass a check. A smaller viewport does not authorize deleting fields, actions or access to full content.

## Inspect and deliver

Look at exactly what you need with `view`, by name: nothing for the whole package; `--tokens` or `--token color`; `--components` or `--component Button` (every variant), with `--variant "Style=secondary"` and `--element Label` for one variant or part; `--pages` or `--page Board`, with `--platform` and `--element`. Choose the form: `--as text` (default outline), `wireframe` for spatial questions, `png` when you can see images and appearance matters, `issues` for layout, text and contrast problems. Check a part after changing it and the whole before delivering: `validate` checks every page version and component variant, and its `issues` include text that does not fit and content wider or taller than its container (`content_overflow`); it cannot judge taste, so look at the PNG of the combinations that matter. A text that fills its slot wraps there and its container grows; several texts in one row hug, so give the one that should take the room `"width": "fill"`. Each write reply's `done` says what changed, by name. Pass `--theme Group/Option` to check a combination; omitting it uses project defaults. Record the targets and combinations you checked in `DESIGN.md`.

Check bounds, text, layout, Token bindings, shared instances and preserved business capabilities. Data validity alone does not prove design quality.

People review the design in the SmallPen App and may fix small things there. Keep the latest `revision` any command reports; before writing code or continuing the design, run `changes PACKAGE --since REVISION` to read, by name, what changed (Tokens with old and new values, component variants and elements, page elements, links) and align your code and notes with it.

Connect the requested clickable elements, triggers and destinations. Use explicit prototype steps to verify navigation. Distinguish page transitions from working input, real data saving or a finished application.

Deliver the package path, retained exports if requested, the targets/combinations actually checked and material limits. Keep one project specification current. Temporary inspection files are not final deliverables. This Skill is independently installable and needs no sibling SmallPen Skill.
